item.title: Version 3.10.7
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.7 — Apologies for the wild ride + introducing the Early-Bird (beta) channel

Today was a marathon: seven stable releases in one afternoon (3.10.0 → 3.10.6) chasing a single bug in the new OpenAI native translation feature. Each was pushed straight to all users because that’s how the update channel was configured. Sorry for the noise — that’s a lot of update prompts in one day.

Going forward, risky changes get their own lane.

  • New: Early-Bird (beta) update channel. Settings → Updates now has a “Receive beta updates” toggle. Flip it on and you’ll see experimental builds (versioned 3.x.y-beta.N) before they ship to everyone — useful if you want to help test fixes early or just like living closer to the edge. Stable users (toggle off, the default) continue to see only fully-vetted releases. You can switch off anytime; the next stable release will pick you back up.
  • This release itself is stable — the toggle is the only feature, no behavior change for the engines or anything else. Nothing forces you onto the beta channel.
  • Built on Sparkle’s native channel-tagging mechanism — clean rollback, clean opt-out, no parallel feeds to maintain.

Tomorrow’s latency-tuning changes (faster post-stop paste, instrumentation, user-controllable wait window) will land first on the beta channel as 3.11.0-beta.1 for early-bird users, then promote to stable once verified. Thanks for your patience today.

item.title: Version 3.10.6
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.6 — Native translation: real fix this time (silence padding)

  • Fixed (for real): the server stopped emitting translated text the moment audio stopped arriving. Per OpenAI’s docs, the dedicated translation endpoint is PURELY continuous — the client never sends commit, close, or response.create events; the server emits deltas while audio (including silence) is arriving and pauses when audio dries up. The previous fixes (longer wait timings, dropping the bogus commit) didn’t help because the issue was upstream: the model had no signal that you’d finished speaking, so it never produced the trailing translation. Now, when you press stop, the engine sends 1 second of zero-PCM silence (5x 200ms chunks) via the same audio-append channel. The model sees a natural end-of-utterance, finalizes the translation, and the engine’s post-stop wait catches all the trailing deltas before delivery.
  • Diagnosis credit: GPT-5 via the codex CLI, after several rounds of wait-timing tweaks failed.
  • Same-language paths and Mini Transcribe / Transcribe are unchanged.

item.title: Version 3.10.5
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.5 — Native translation now actually waits for the full translation

  • Fixed (for real this time): trailing translated text being cut off when you press stop. Two issues compounded: (a) we were sending an input_audio_buffer.commit event to nudge the server, but per OpenAI’s documentation translate sessions are purely continuous and the client never signals turn boundaries — that event was likely silently erroring on the translate endpoint and cutting subsequent deltas short. Removed. (b) The post-stop wait timings were too aggressive: a 1.5s pre-start window (raised to 3s) and 0.8s post-start quiet window (raised to 1.5s), both insufficient for the real latency of the translate model. Hard cap raised from 8s to 12s.
  • What this means in practice: when you press stop, audio capture halts but the WebSocket stays alive and the engine keeps receiving translated tokens from the server. The wait loop only releases when the model has genuinely gone quiet for 1.5 seconds, or fired its explicit completion event, or 12 seconds have passed. Whatever you saw streaming live in the pill is what lands in the paste.
  • Same-language English-to-English on Mini Transcribe / Transcribe is unchanged.

item.title: Version 3.10.4
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.4 — Native translation actually waits for the translation to finish

  • Fixed: trailing words still cropped on the translate path even after 3.10.3. The previous fix drained our local audio queue before the server commit (correct) but the post-commit wait was naive: it exited after 500ms of “no new server event,” which can fire DURING the model’s pre-response gap — before any translated text has even started arriving. Translation then exited before it began.
  • Two-phase wait now: (1) wait up to 1.5s for the server’s first response after stop — if nothing arrives, the server really has nothing more to say; (2) once streaming has begun, wait for it to actually go quiet (800ms after the last delta) OR for an explicit completion event. Hard cap at 8s for genuinely stuck cases. The translated text you see streaming live in the pill IS what gets pasted — nothing trailing gets dropped anymore.
  • Same-language English-to-English on Mini Transcribe / Transcribe is unchanged — this only affects the “Translate live via OpenAI Realtime” path.

item.title: Version 3.10.3
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.3 — Fix: trailing words dropped from cloud transcripts + clearer engine names

  • Fixed: the last word (or two) of every cloud-engine dictation was being cropped from the paste. Root cause was a race in our audio pipeline: AVAudioEngine.stop() halts the mic tap callback, but audio chunks already queued for conversion + send were still in flight when we told the server “commit everything you have.” Server committed without the last ~200-400ms of speech. Both OpenAIRealtimeEngine and OpenAITranslateEngine had the same race; the translate engine’s shorter wait made it visible. Now we drain our local audio queue before sending commit, so every captured chunk reaches the server first.
  • Translate stop is also smarter about waiting. Replaced the fixed 1.2s post-commit wait with a quiescence-based wait: exit when the server’s done event arrives OR when no new event has arrived for 500ms (after a minimum 200ms). Caps total wait at 2.5s. Result: tighter lag in the common case, catches genuinely-late deltas in the edge case.
  • Engine names disambiguated. “OpenAI Whisper” (the local whisper.cpp engine that runs offline on your Mac) is now “Whisper (local, offline)”. “OpenAI Realtime” is now “OpenAI Realtime (cloud)”. The new realtime sub-model “Whisper Streaming” is now “Realtime Whisper (cloud, low-latency)” with a clearer cost note (~5-6x more expensive than Mini). No behavior change — just easier to tell which Whisper is which.

item.title: Version 3.10.2
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.2 — Faster paste on native translation + no more dropped trailing words

  • Translation paste is significantly faster. The dedicated translation session streams continuously and only fires “final” events at model-detected sentence boundaries — not when you stop talking. 3.10.0/3.10.1 waited up to 5 seconds for a final that often never came. Now we nudge the server to flush trailing audio on stop, wait at most 1.2 seconds, and promote any in-flight partial to the final if needed. Result: paste happens roughly when you expect it instead of after a 5-second pause.
  • Trailing words no longer dropped. If you stopped mid-sentence, the last few words could be lost because they were buffered in a partial that never received a finalization event. They’re now folded into the delivered text.
  • Same-language English-to-English on Mini Transcribe / Transcribe is unchanged — this only affects the “Translate live via OpenAI Realtime” per-profile path.

item.title: Version 3.10.1
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.1 — Fix: legacy OpenAI Realtime models produced empty results in 3.10.0

  • Fixed: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe dictation came back empty. 3.10.0 migrated the OpenAI Realtime engine to the GA endpoint (dropping the legacy OpenAI-Beta header) but kept sending the old transcription_session.update event shape for the legacy models. The GA endpoint silently ignores that event, so those models had no transcription configured and produced no transcripts — the overlay said “Delivered” with no text inserted. Native translation (gpt-realtime-translate) and Whisper Streaming were unaffected.
  • All three OpenAI Realtime models now use the GA session.update shape. Same-language English-to-English dictation works again on Mini Transcribe (the default) and Transcribe.
  • If you were stuck on 3.10.0 with the default settings, this hotfix restores normal behavior. Translation users who were happy with 3.10.0 see no change.

item.title: Version 3.10.0
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.10.0 — New OpenAI realtime models + native live translation

  • New OpenAI Realtime model: Whisper Streaming. Added gpt-realtime-whisper (released by OpenAI on May 7, 2026) as a third option in the OpenAI Realtime model picker. Optimized for low-latency live transcription with strong handling of accents and noisy audio. Sends your profile’s input language as a hint to the model for better quality on non-English dictation. Mini Transcribe remains the default; Whisper Streaming is opt-in for users who want lowest latency or better multilingual handling.
  • New: Native live translation via OpenAI Realtime. Per-profile toggle “Translate live via OpenAI Realtime (low-latency)”. When enabled and the profile’s output language differs from the input language, dictation streams through OpenAI’s dedicated gpt-realtime-translate endpoint — transcription and translation happen in a single streaming pass instead of transcribe→then→LLM-translate. Result: roughly 1–2 seconds faster perceived latency on cross-lingual dictation (e.g. Bulgarian or Russian or Spanish → English). Uses ~$0.034/min while active vs. ~$0.007/min on the default same-language path; off by default, enable per profile.
  • Migrated to OpenAI’s GA Realtime API. Dropped the legacy OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1 header. Existing models (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe) continue to work unchanged on the GA endpoint.
  • Default behavior unchanged. Same-language users on the default Mini Transcribe model see no behavioral change — just a smoother backend.

item.title: Version 3.9.0
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.9.0 — Custom presets, smarter app selector, faster GPT-5, in-app updates fixed

  • Custom AI presets — create as many as you want, name them yourself. Instead of a single "Custom..." slot, the AI preset picker now has a "Your Custom Presets" section where you can save reusable named prompts ("Email tone", "Slack casual", "Bullet points punchy", etc.). The same preset can be selected across multiple profiles — edit once, applies everywhere it's used. A "+ New custom preset…" option in the picker opens an editor sheet with name + prompt + Save/Delete. Existing custom prompts are migrated automatically.
  • App selector now finds anything you have open. Previously the App dropdown only listed a hardcoded set of common apps. Now it includes every currently running user-visible app (so Obsidian, Linear, Notion, anything open right now is selectable directly) plus a folder-icon button that opens the Applications folder so you can pick any installed app, running or not.
  • GPT-5 family now runs at minimal reasoning effort. For dictation cleanup the task is short and structural — no internal reasoning needed. Result: noticeably faster responses and lower cost for the same output quality.
  • Settings → Updates → Check for Updates button: third attempt, different shape. Refactored the updater into a shared singleton accessed identically by the menu bar and the in-app button (no more NSApp.delegate cast). Uses Sparkle's official SwiftUI integration pattern with observed state. Shows on-screen status after a check — if for any reason no Sparkle alert appears, the status line confirms the click fired.

item.title: Version 3.8.3
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.8.3 — GPT-5 models work + in-app updates really fixed

  • Fixed: GPT-5 family models returned API error 400. The 3.8.1 picker added gpt-5-nano/gpt-5-mini/gpt-5 but they all rejected the request body. GPT-5 family and o-series reasoning models don't accept the legacy temperature and max_tokens parameters — they require max_completion_tokens and only the default temperature. The request shape now switches per model so all picker options work.
  • Fixed (really): Settings → Updates → Check for Updates button. 3.8.2 corrected the API call but missed the activation step. Sonotexta is a menu-bar app and the Settings window lives in a non-main window, so Sparkle's alert was appearing behind it — visually identical to "nothing happens". Now the app activates before the check, so the alert surfaces on top.

item.title: Version 3.8.2
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.8.2 — In-app updates fixed + release history refresh

  • Fixed: Settings → Updates → Check for Updates button. It was silently doing nothing — only the menu bar's Check for Updates… worked. Both paths now show the standard Sparkle update panel.
  • In-app release history is current. Was showing old hardcoded entries (and even a phantom v3.2.5 that never existed). Now lists 3.6 through this release, matching the website and the auto-update feed.
  • Removed the misleading "You're on the latest version" static text — the app couldn't actually verify that without checking. The version + build are still shown; Check for Updates does the real verification.

item.title: Version 3.8.1
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.8.1 — Refreshed OpenAI model picker

  • GPT-5 family added. The AI post-processing picker now includes gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini, and gpt-5 alongside the existing GPT-4 family. gpt-5-nano is the new default for direct OpenAI users — at $0.05 input / $0.40 output per 1M tokens it's the cheapest model in the active OpenAI lineup, perfect for the short cleanup/translate prompts dictation generates.
  • Picker now flags pricing tiers explicitly. The descriptions tell you which model is cheapest where: "Cheapest overall — newer family" for gpt-5-nano, and "Cheapest mini tier — well-tested" for gpt-4o-mini (which is still the cheapest in the "mini" tier at $0.15/$0.60).
  • Cloud subscribers (managed proxy) move from gpt-4.1-mini to gpt-5-mini — newer family with similar cost profile.
  • Existing user choices are preserved: if you'd already picked a specific model, you stay on it. The default change only affects users who hadn't picked one.
  • Speech-to-text engines untouched — gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe are still current and stay as the realtime options.

item.title: Version 3.8
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.8 — Brand-aligned downloads

  • Download files now match the product name. Each release ships as Sonotexta-X.Y.Z.dmg instead of the legacy VoiceFlow.dmg. Cosmetic, but also fixes a real propagation issue: when several versions ship close together, the same generic filename could leave some users' Sparkle stuck on an intermediate version because their CDN edge had cached a stale combination. Each version now has its own unique download URL, so cache contamination is impossible.
  • No functional changes — same app, just a cleaner filename and more reliable update propagation.

item.title: Version 3.7.3
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.7.3 — Multiple contacts per app in one profile

  • One profile, many contacts. You can now attach as many specific contacts as you like to a single profile within the same app — no more creating ten near-identical profiles for ten different colleagues. Each app card now has an Add another contact button, so a single "Work English" profile can match Filip, Markus, and Andreas in Teams (and the same colleagues in Slack, if you add them there too).
  • The profile list now shows all apps a profile targets in its subtitle, not just the first one.

item.title: Version 3.7.2
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.7.2 — Smarter profile matching

  • Contact-specific profiles now beat app-wide profiles automatically. Before, if you had a "Teams → German" profile and added a "Filip in Teams → English" profile later, Filip's messages still came out in German because the matcher used profile order. Now the matcher checks specificity: a profile that targets a specific contact in an app always wins over a profile that targets the whole app, regardless of when each was added. You can keep adding contact-specific profiles without manually reordering.

item.title: Version 3.7.1
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.7.1 — Hotfix for paste regression

  • Fixed: in 3.7, transcribed text could end up on the clipboard without actually pasting into the focused app (especially in Terminal, iTerm, and Electron-based apps like VS Code or Claude Code). The new direct-insertion attempt was reporting success while doing nothing visible. Reverted to clipboard paste as the primary delivery path — matches 3.6 behavior. All other 3.7 improvements (durable last-dictation store, menu bar recovery actions, honest delivery status, safer clipboard restore, Apple Speech finalization fix, realtime engine race fix) remain in place.

item.title: Version 3.7
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.7 — Delivery reliability + engine race fix

You never lose a transcription again

  • Last Dictation recovery — every transcription is now saved durably. New menu bar items: Paste Last Dictation (⌃⇧V), Copy Last Dictation (⌃⇧C), Show Last Dictation
  • Honest delivery status — the overlay no longer says “Delivered” when paste might have silently failed. You’ll see Copied — paste manually when delivery isn’t certain
  • Layered insertion — tries direct Accessibility insertion first, falls back to clipboard paste, falls back to leave-in-clipboard. More reliable across apps with Secure Input or restricted text fields
  • Safer clipboard restore — we no longer overwrite your clipboard with stale content if you copied something else right after dictating

Engine race fix

  • Fixed: short utterances with Apple Speech sometimes lost the final transcription — replaced abort with proper end-of-audio + finalization wait
  • Fixed: realtime engines (OpenAI Realtime, Deepgram) could deliver an empty buffer if the final event arrived a fraction of a second late on stop. Engines now return the final text directly, eliminating the race
  • Cleaner internals — each engine now owns its own transcript accumulator, removing duplicated state in the dictation manager

item.title: Version 3.6
item.description:
Sonotexta 3.6

  • Multi-app detection rules — one profile can match across iMessage, Teams, Slack, etc. with different contact names per app
  • Fixed: profiles no longer lost on update (migration-safe decoder for new fields)
  • Improved mic sharing — proper voice processing API with progressive retry for FaceTime/Zoom
  • Input language per profile — tell the speech engine and AI what language you’re speaking for better accuracy on short phrases and similar languages
  • Improved FaceTime/Zoom mic sharing — voice processing API for reliable concurrent mic access
  • Updates tab — release history and check for updates from Settings
  • Support page — privacy, terms, website, and contact links in Settings
  • Fixed: dictation now stops reliably with local engines (Whisper, Parakeet)
  • Fixed: AI no longer interprets your dictation as instructions
  • Fixed: duplicate default profiles can now be deleted
  • Clearer AI setup — Ollama highlighted as free local option
  • Sonotexta AI and Cloud subscriptions, 8 AI presets, microphone selection, dictation stats
